FenceStatements is what a resolved lock or row WriteFencePlan carries as its sql field, derived from FenceSql by resolveFenceStatements; no code ever hand-authors one. requireWriteFence accepts WriteFencePlan as a parameter, which this checker treats as an author-facing position for every member mandatory on every variant. acquireKeyed/acquireKeyedWithIsolation replace the deleted advisoryLock/advisoryLockWithIsolation names (already exempted here before the rename) as the mechanism-neutral forms every keyed lock site now calls.

ResolvedSqlTableNames is the fully-resolved table-name set createSqlSchema returns and GraphBackend.tableNames exposes; fences (default "typegraph_fences") joins it as part of the base schema so the row write-fence mechanism can spell its acquire statement through the query builder. The corresponding SqlTableNames input field is optional and defaults, so a caller constructing a schema or table-name override is unaffected; only code that builds a complete ResolvedSqlTableNames object literal by hand (rather than through createSqlSchema/a bundled backend factory) must add it.

the query builder's subclass-expansion axis moves from a boolean `includeSubClasses` to a resolved `AliasExpansionAxis`, so the builder's internal state carries `startExpansion` / `expansion` and its config carries the store-level `defaultIncludeSubClasses`, and a supertype alias resolves to `PolymorphicNodeType`. None of `QueryBuilderConfig`, `QueryBuilderState`, `QueryStart` or `PolymorphicNodeType` is exported from any entrypoint; they are the builder's internal state, reached only because the builder class constructors appear in the report. Declared in .changeset/typed-subsumption.md.

`StoreRuntime` is the `@internal`, symbol-keyed store runtime port documented as absent from the public `Store` contract; it is not exported from any entrypoint, so no external consumer can name or author one. Declared in .changeset/typed-subsumption.md.

EngineRevision is the opaque token backend.lineage.revision()/changesSince() exchange; no code ever hand-constructs one, matching NodeId/RecordedInstant's own established brand pattern. LineageMembers.changesSince declares revision as a parameter, and lineage is a brand-new optional GraphBackend member, but the checker's brand-new-callable gating (existingCallableKeys/calleeExisted) only recognizes interface method-signature syntax, not the arrow-typed property style BackendCatalogProbes/LineageMembers use for `this: void` receiver-free members, so the parameter is walked as though the member were pre-existing and its required brand becomes a false-positive breaking change.
